title: Brackenreach after the restoration
story_basis: docs/full-story.md section11: forest changed not destroyed, moved roads, some collapsed bridges, newly open paths; hollow-tree village; Hearthlight relit softer amber guide, safe crossing markers/messages, new maps.

docs/full-story.md section2: Brackenreach around enormous hollow tree, wooden homes/upper bridges, central tall wooden Hearthlight frame. Restoration layer shapes and props below are proposals; not a rigid reset.
review_notes: Environment proposal/prototype; no production approval or runtime integration inferred.
Interactive art states below are production interpretations, not newly established story mechanics.

deliverables.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Lanterns Underroot hand-painted illustrated 2D side-scrolling platformer asset. Input images ART-001/002/006 are style, palette, material and layer-separation references ONLY; ignore their text, logos, characters, guide panels and layouts. Match rich painterly wood/stone/foliage, selective crisp silhouettes, restrained brush texture, warm amber light against forest greens and cool blue-teal shadows. Strict SIDE-ON game camera, no isometric view or forced vanishing-point perspective on usable surfaces. No player, NPC, enemy, UI, logo, watermark, labels or text. Brackenreach after restoration: same hollow-tree woodland village identity, warm hopeful evening, living moving forest, newly opened path gaps, some old crossing remains, softer amber Hearthlight guiding rather than restraining roots. Primary request: ONE 1536x1024 composed side-on environment LIGHTING STUDY of Brackenreach after the restoration. Hopeful dusk woodland village, warm softer amber lantern light along routes, natural green foliage and cool blue shadows. Light guides travelers rather than holding roots still; no catastrophic forest destruction. Show one coherent representative location view without characters; no panels, guide text, logos or atlas. It may combine environment layers solely to demonstrate intended light/depth. This is explicitly an art reference, NOT a runtime layer, terrain atlas, flattened substitute for the other seven deliverables, or production-ready level.
